repeated.title: Which credential the operator holds to read customers and publish

1.1.title: Which credential the operator preparing a client message holds
1.1.quote: | read a customer | staff, operator preparing a client message | name, phone, e-mail, language |
behaviours: The operator (the Factory agent building the WhatsApp link) is treated as staff and is issued the staff credential, with full write access to customers and projects.

The operator gets its own read-only credential (or a service token) that may read a customer but nothing else; R0-09 is read as allowing this although it says reading a customer needs the staff credential.
1.1.who_notices: The owner, when the Factory agent either cannot read the phone for the WhatsApp link or turns out to hold a credential that can erase customers.

1.2.title: Credential of the operator script onboard_object
1.2.quote:
Cabinet Kernel
  and the operator also create projects and rooms, and publish artifacts as
  producers (below). They reach Registry over HTTP on the host's loopback or
  private network; a service that writes holds a service token (R0-09).
behaviours: onboard_object authenticates with the staff credential (it is listed under Owner / staff) and therefore cannot publish artifacts, because publishing requires the owner service to be the service the token names.
onboard_object holds a service token naming an 'operator' service, which then must appear as an owner in the configured vocabulary for the types it publishes.
1.2.who_notices: The operator, when onboarding fails at the publish step, or the instance administrator configuring tokens.

2.1.title: Operator reading a customer: which credential and which actor
2.1.quote: | read a customer | staff, operator preparing a client message | name, phone, e-mail, language |
behaviours: The operator is treated as staff and reads with the staff credential, so the Factory agent holds the staff credential
The operator is a separate caller with its own service token that may read customers, so R0-09's 'needs the staff credential' gets an exception
2.1.who_notices: The owner, when the Factory's WhatsApp link step cannot read the phone, or when an agent turns out to hold the staff credential

2.2.title: Operator script publishing artifacts: token or staff credential
2.2.quote:
The owner service
  must be the service the caller's token names, and the type must belong to
  that service (R0-08, R0-09).
behaviours: onboard_object gets its own service token that names an owner service, and publishes only that service's types
onboard_object uses the staff credential, and staff may publish any type, with the owner service taken from the request
2.2.who_notices: The operator, when onboard_object's publish is refused, or a reviewer, when staff can publish another service's pointer

3.1.title: Who the 'operator preparing a client message' is and which credential it holds
3.1.quote: | read a customer | staff, operator preparing a client message | name, phone, e-mail, language |
behaviours: The operator (the Factory agent that builds the WhatsApp link) is treated as staff and reads with the staff credential; no separate actor or credential exists
The operator is a distinct caller with its own service token allowed to read contact data, which contradicts R0-09 and 'readable by staff only' unless that is an exception
3.1.who_notices: Owner when the Factory agent cannot read the phone, or security review finding a non-staff token reading personal data

3.7.title: Which credential the operator script and consumer services use for which writes
3.7.unit: R0-09 — Writes and contact data need a credential (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-04, replaces L15)
3.7.quote: Each writing service holds a service token that names it; staff hold a staff credential. Every write needs one of them;
behaviours: Any valid token of either kind may perform any write; the 'who' column is descriptive only (a consumer token can correct or archive a project, staff can publish)

Credential kind is enforced per action: correct/archive/customer need staff, publish/withdraw need a service token naming the owner; `onboard_object` therefore holds both a staff credential and its own service token

repeated.title: Is the 'who' column enforced by credential kind (e.g. listing rooms)

1.3.title: Whether the 'who' column is enforced by credential kind
1.3.quote:
Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or
erasing a customer needs the staff credential.
behaviours: Any valid credential (service token or staff) may perform every project write; a consumer service may correct or archive a project, since only customer actions are reserved to staff.
Each write accepts only the credential kinds named in the table's 'who' column: correct/archive project with a service token is refused; publish/withdraw with the staff credential is refused.
1.3.who_notices: Staff, when a consumer service archives a project; or a security review of the service tokens.

2.13.title: Who may list rooms after R0-09
2.13.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order |
behaviours: Listing rooms is open to any caller, like 'read a project', which already returns the rooms
Listing rooms needs a staff credential or a service token
2.13.who_notices: An unauthenticated reader (e.g. the browser) whose room list is refused while the project card shows rooms

repeated.title: Staff credential: one shared secret or one per person; who issues it

1.6.title: One shared staff credential or one per person
behaviours: One shared staff secret in the instance configuration; Registry cannot tell which staff member acted and cannot revoke one person.
Per-person staff credentials, with Registry recording which staff member made each write or read of contact data.
1.6.who_notices: The owner, when a staff member leaves, or when asked who read or erased a customer's personal data.

2.9.title: Staff credential: one shared secret or one per person
2.9.unit: R0-09 — Writes and contact data need a credential (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-04, replaces L15)
behaviours: One staff credential per instance in the protected configuration, shared by everyone on staff
One credential per staff member, so Registry knows which person recorded, corrected or erased a customer
2.9.who_notices: The owner, when someone leaves and the credential must be revoked, or when asked who erased a customer

3.8.title: What a staff credential is and who issues and checks it
3.8.quote:
They
  authenticate with a staff credential (R0-09); today no route authenticates
  anyone (L15).
behaviours: One shared staff secret in the instance's protected configuration, checked by Registry; actions are not attributable to a person
Per-person staff credentials issued by an external identity system that Registry trusts, which is then an unnamed external system and trust boundary
3.8.who_notices: Owner when a staff member leaves or an audit asks who erased a customer

repeated.title: Is the customer's name erasable contact data

1.8.title: Is the customer's name contact data
1.8.quote:
Registry holds a Customer record: who the project is for and how to reach
them — name, phone, e-mail, language.
behaviours: Name is contact data: it is erased with the rest and is readable by staff only, so the open project card and context carry only customer_ref.
Name is identity, not contact data: it survives erasure and may appear in the open project card / context; only phone, e-mail and language are erased and protected.
1.8.who_notices: The customer who asked for erasure and is still named; or Client Portal, which shows a customer name taken from context.

2.3.title: Is the customer's name contact data or project identity
2.3.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
2.3.quote:
how to reach
them — name, phone, e-mail, language.
behaviours: The name is contact data: readable by staff only, wiped on erasure, and the open project card and context carry only customer_ref
The name stays identity: the open project card and context still show the customer's name, and erasure removes only phone, e-mail and language
2.3.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which read the 'customer' field of context, and the owner during an erasure request

3.3.title: Is the customer's name part of the erasable contact data
3.3.quote: | erase a customer's contact data | staff | the Customer keeps its identity, its contact data is gone; projects still name it (R0-06) | unknown customer refused |
behaviours: Name, phone, e-mail and language are all erased; only `customer_ref` survives
Phone and e-mail are erased but name (and language) remain so projects still show who the customer was
3.3.who_notices: Staff looking at an old project, and the data subject who asked for erasure

repeated.title: Must a project's customer_ref name an existing Customer

1.10.title: Must a project's customer_ref name an existing Customer
1.10.quote: | correct a project | staff | the project with the new name, address or customer | unknown id refused; an archived project refused (R0-12) |
behaviours: Creating or correcting a project with a customer_ref that names no Customer (or an erased one) is refused; existing projects with free-text customer_ref must be migrated first.
customer_ref stays an unchecked reference; a project may name a customer not (yet) recorded, and the read of that customer answers unknown.
1.10.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel creating projects before staff record the customer; the operator preparing a WhatsApp link that finds no customer.

2.4.title: Creating or correcting a project with a customer_ref that names no Customer
2.4.quote: | create a project | staff, consumer service | the project with its identity — supplied by the caller or minted (R0-07) — status `active` | missing name or address refused;
behaviours: An unknown customer_ref is refused, so Cabinet Kernel (which cannot record or read customers) needs a staff-recorded customer before it can create a project
customer_ref is accepted unchecked, and a project may name a Customer that does not exist or does not exist yet
2.4.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel, when its project creation starts failing; the owner, when the WhatsApp link finds no customer

3.4.title: Must a project's customer reference name an existing Customer
3.4.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
3.4.quote: `customer_ref` becomes the Customer's identity, and a project names its customer by it.
behaviours: Create and correct refuse a `customer_ref` that is not a recorded Customer; existing projects with free-text refs must be migrated first
`customer_ref` stays an unchecked string; a project may name a customer that has no Customer record and 'read a customer' answers unknown
3.4.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel / operator creating projects with today's refs; owner when the WhatsApp link finds no customer

2.5.title: Existing projects whose customer_ref predates the Customer record
2.5.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
2.5.quote:
`customer_ref` becomes the Customer's
identity, and a project names its customer by it.
behaviours: Every existing customer_ref value becomes a Customer record with only a name (or none), created at migration
Existing values stay as dangling references until staff record a Customer by hand; reading such a customer answers unknown
2.5.who_notices: Staff and the operator, the first time they read the customer of an existing project

repeated.title: No action finds or lists customers

1.11.title: No action finds or lists customers
behaviours: Staff can only reach a Customer by a known customer_ref (from a project); duplicates are recorded because nobody can look up an existing customer.
A 'list/search customers' action is added (staff only) although no promise carries it.
1.11.who_notices: Staff attaching an existing customer to a new project; the owner seeing duplicate customers.

2.6.title: No way to find a Customer
behaviours: A 'list customers' (or search by name) action for staff is added, so the frontend can pick a customer when creating a project
Staff must already know the customer_ref; there is no listing, and duplicates of one person are recorded
2.6.who_notices: Staff using the Registry frontend to attach a customer to a project

3.5.title: No action to find or list customers
behaviours: Staff find a customer only through a project's `customer_ref`; no list or search of customers exists
A 'list customers' (staff only) is added so staff can pick an existing customer instead of recording a duplicate
3.5.who_notices: Staff recording a repeat customer twice

repeated.title: Erase vs anonymise; repeating an erasure

1.12.title: Erase versus anonymise
1.12.quote: can be erased or anonymised: an explicit exception to R0-03, the only one.
behaviours: Erasure removes the contact fields; the read answers 'erased' with no data (as in the table).
Anonymisation replaces the fields with placeholder values, and the read returns those placeholders as an ordinary customer, or the two are separate actions.
1.12.who_notices: The operator preparing a client message, who either gets 'erased' or a placeholder phone; the customer exercising erasure.

2.8.title: Erased versus anonymised
2.8.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
2.8.quote: can be erased or anonymised: an explicit exception to R0-03, the only one.
behaviours: The contact fields are removed and the Customer is marked erased, as the 'read a customer' row says
The fields are replaced with placeholder values and the Customer reads as an ordinary record without an erased marker
2.8.who_notices: The operator preparing a WhatsApp link, who either gets 'erased' or a placeholder phone

3.6.title: Repeating an erasure
3.6.quote: | erase a customer's contact data | staff | the Customer keeps its identity, its contact data is gone; projects still name it (R0-06) | unknown customer refused |
behaviours: Erasing an already-erased customer returns it unchanged (as archive does, R0-12)
Erasing an already-erased customer is refused, like correcting one
3.6.who_notices: Staff or a retrying operator script

repeated.title: Create replay with the id of a corrected or archived project

1.14.title: Replay of a create after the project was corrected or archived
1.14.quote:
A repeated create
with that id and equal content returns the existing project; with different
content it is refused, and nothing changes.
behaviours: Equal content is compared with the project's current state: a replay of the original create after a correction is refused, and a replay against an archived project returns it archived.
Equal content is compared with the original create request: the replay succeeds after a correction, while a replay against an archived project is refused because the project is archived.
1.14.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel retrying a create after staff corrected the address.

2.11.title: Create replay of an id whose project is now archived
2.11.quote: an equal replay returns the existing project, a different one with the same id is refused (R0-07)
behaviours: An equal replay returns the archived project as it is, status archived
The replay is refused because the project is archived (R0-12: archive is final)
2.11.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel or onboard_object retrying a create, which then either proceeds with an archived project or fails

3.10.title: Create with the id of an archived project
3.10.unit: R0-07 — The caller may supply a project's identity (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-02, replaces V1-5, L01, L02)
3.10.quote:
A repeated create
with that id and equal content returns the existing project; with different
content it is refused, and nothing changes.
behaviours: An equal replay returns the archived project as it is (status `archived`)
The create is refused because the project is archived and the caller expected an `active` project
3.10.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel or a second instance re-onboarding an object

repeated.title: Pointers whose type or owner left the configured vocabulary

1.15.title: Pointers whose type or owner left the configured vocabulary
1.15.quote:
The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are
a list in the instance's configuration, not in the specification
behaviours: Removing a type, or changing its owner, affects only new publishes; existing pointers stay readable and are withdrawable by the service named on the pointer.
Pointers of a type no longer listed are hidden or no longer withdrawable, and after an owner change only the new owner may withdraw them.
1.15.who_notices: A consumer listing history after the administrator edits the vocabulary; a producer that can no longer withdraw its pointer.

2.10.title: Pointers whose type leaves the configured vocabulary or changes owner
2.10.unit: R0-08 — The artifact vocabulary is configured, one owner per type (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-03, replaces L08)
2.10.quote:
The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are
a list in the instance's configuration, not in the specification: adding a type
needs no spec change.
behaviours: Existing pointers stay listed and readable, and stay withdrawable by the service named on the pointer
Pointers of an unlisted type are hidden or refused on read, and only the type's current owner may withdraw
2.10.who_notices: A consumer reading history after the configuration changes; a producer whose withdraw is refused

3.11.title: Owner of existing pointers after the configured vocabulary changes
3.11.unit: R0-08 — The artifact vocabulary is configured, one owner per type (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-03, replaces L08)
3.11.quote:
The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are
a list in the instance's configuration, not in the specification: adding a type
needs no spec change.
behaviours: Pointers keep the owner service recorded at publish; only that service may withdraw, even after configuration moves or removes the type
Ownership is taken from the current configuration; after a change the new owner withdraws, and pointers of a removed type can no longer be withdrawn or are hidden
3.11.who_notices: Producer service refused when withdrawing its own old pointer

repeated.title: Withdrawing a pointer of an archived project

1.16.title: Withdrawing a pointer of an archived project
1.16.quote: | withdraw an artifact pointer | the producer service that owns it | the pointer, status `withdrawn`; it stays in the history (R0-14) | unknown pointer refused; a pointer of another service, or already withdrawn or superseded, refused |
behaviours: Withdrawal is allowed on an archived project, so a producer can mark a deleted artifact even after archiving.
Withdrawal is a write to an archived project and is refused, like publishing and adding a room.
1.16.who_notices: A producer that deleted the artifact of an archived project; a consumer still reading the stale published pointer.

3.9.title: Withdrawing a pointer of an archived project
3.9.quote: | withdraw an artifact pointer | the producer service that owns it | the pointer, status `withdrawn`; it stays in the history (R0-14) | unknown pointer refused; a pointer of another service, or already withdrawn or superseded, refused |
behaviours: Withdraw is allowed on an archived project, since the artifact may be deleted after archiving
Withdraw is refused on an archived project, like publish
3.9.who_notices: A producer that deleted an artifact of an archived project and leaves a stale `published` pointer

repeated.title: What the open project card and context carry as 'customer'

1.9.title: What the project card and context carry as 'customer' now
1.9.quote: | read a project context | consumer service | the snapshot a consumer keeps: id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times | unknown id refused |
behaviours: 'customer' stays exactly the v1 value (R0-04), now interpreted as the Customer's customer_ref; no contact data is embedded.
'customer' is filled from the Customer record (e.g. its name), so open, unauthenticated reads expose personal data.
1.9.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which pin the context fields; a privacy review of open reads.

3.2.title: Does the open project card / context expose customer contact data
3.2.quote: Reading projects, rooms, artifacts, `validate` and `context` needs no credential there; every write and every read of contact data does (R0-09).
behaviours: The project card and context carry only `customer_ref` (the customer's name is not shown), so open reads never reveal personal data
The context keeps its existing customer field field-for-field (R0-04) and fills it with the Customer's name or contact data, so an unauthenticated read returns personal data
3.2.who_notices: PresuPro / Client Portal when the customer field changes meaning, or a privacy review

single.title: Can staff publish or withdraw a pointer
single.quote: | withdraw an artifact pointer | the producer service that owns it |
behaviours: Only a service token whose service owns the pointer may withdraw it; staff cannot clean up a stale pointer whose producer is gone.
The staff credential may withdraw (and publish) any pointer on behalf of its owner service.
single.who_notices: Staff, when a producer service is retired and its stale published pointer cannot be removed.

single.title: Where the per-service tokens and their service names are stored
single.quote:
- **Secrets** — service tokens and the staff credential, in the instance's
  protected configuration; never in a record, a log line or an answer.
behaviours: The configuration maps each token to a service name that must also appear in the R0-08 vocabulary; a token for an unlisted service is rejected at start-up.
Tokens and the vocabulary are independent lists; a token may name any service string and only publishing checks the vocabulary.
single.who_notices: The instance administrator, when adding a new consumer service that writes but publishes nothing.

single.title: Reachability outside loopback and the private network
behaviours: The service binds only to loopback/private interfaces; nothing outside is ever served, so the Browser frontend must also be on the private network.
The service may be exposed beyond the private network, where reads also require a credential ('there' limits only where reads are open).
single.who_notices: Staff opening the Registry frontend from outside the office network; the operator deploying the instance.

single.title: Customer identity across instances
single.quote:
One physical object can therefore carry one id across instances
(R0-05).
behaviours: Only the project_id may be caller-supplied; each instance mints its own customer_ref, so the same project created in two instances has different customer content and an equal replay cannot succeed across them.
The caller may also supply customer_ref when recording a customer, so the same customer carries one identity across instances.
single.who_notices: The operator replicating a project between instances, whose replay is refused as different content.

single.title: Correcting a customer: overwrite or keep the earlier contact data
single.quote: | correct a customer | staff | the Customer with the new contact data |
behaviours: The new contact data overwrites the old; nothing earlier is kept, so erasure has one place to wipe
Earlier values are kept as history (as Registry otherwise never deletes), and erasure must also wipe every earlier version
single.who_notices: The customer or the owner during an erasure request, when old phone numbers survive

single.title: Superseded pointer whose artifact the producer deleted
single.quote: a pointer of another service, or already withdrawn or superseded, refused
behaviours: A superseded pointer can never be withdrawn; the history keeps pointing at a deleted artifact without any mark
A producer may withdraw any of its pointers that is not already withdrawn, including superseded ones
single.who_notices: A consumer reading artifact history and following a dead uri
